myth: The fierce form of the Divine Mother who arose to destroy demons such as Raktabija; she is linked to time, death and the liberation of the soul from ego.
wants: Pride and illusion cut away; the helpless defended from those who prey on them

myth: A warrior goddess formed from the combined radiance of the gods to defeat the buffalo demon Mahishasura; her victory is celebrated at Navaratri and Durga Puja.
wants: Demons and tyrants faced down; the weak sheltered behind her contractors' shields

myth: The monkey-faced devotee of Rama and son of the wind god, who leapt the ocean to Lanka and carried a mountain of healing herbs; he embodies strength, humility and devotion.
wants: Devotion proven through service; strength used only for the good of others

myth: The eighth avatar of Vishnu, beloved as the flute-playing cowherd of Vrindavan and as the charioteer who taught the Bhagavad Gita to Arjuna at Kurukshetra.
wants: Duty done without attachment; joy, music and devotion shared freely

myth: The seventh avatar of Vishnu and hero of the Ramayana, the ideal king who kept his word through fourteen years of exile and rescued Sita from the demon king Ravana.
wants: Promises kept at any cost; just rule and faithful households

myth: The Vedic god of fire and the sacrificial flame, the messenger who carries offerings from mortals to the gods and dwells in every hearth.
wants: Offerings given with sincerity; sacred fires kept lit

myth: The first mortal to die, who became lord of the dead and judge of souls; he rides a buffalo, carries a noose and upholds dharma.
wants: Souls sent on at their proper hour; the dead judged by their deeds

myth: The six-faced son of Shiva and Parvati, also called Skanda and Murugan, born to lead the army of the gods against the demon Taraka; he rides a peacock and bears the Vel spear.
wants: Armies led with discipline; young warriors trained and tested

myth: The Vedic god of wind and breath, the life-force that moves through all beings, and father of Hanuman and Bhima.
wants: Breath honoured and air kept clean; messages carried fast

myth: King of the yakshas and treasurer of the gods, guardian of the north and of the hidden riches of the earth, who once ruled the golden city of Lanka.
wants: Treasures guarded and honestly counted; debts repaid in full

myth: The moon god who drives a chariot drawn by antelopes; his waxing and waning came from a curse by Daksha, and he is linked to soma, the nectar of the gods.
wants: Calm minds and honest marriages; what was lost allowed to wax again

myth: The god of love and desire who shoots flower-tipped arrows from a sugarcane bow; burned to ash by Shiva's third eye, he was later reborn.
wants: Love kindled between those meant for it; desire honoured, never forced

myth: The sacred river Ganges in divine form, who descended from heaven through Shiva's locks to purify the ashes of King Sagara's sons; her waters wash away sin.
wants: Rivers kept clean; the dead given proper rites and peace

myth: The divine craftsman and architect who built the cities, chariots and weapons of the gods, including golden Lanka and Krishna's Dwarka.
wants: Tools respected and buildings raised true; craftsmanship taught
relic: Measuring Rod of the Divine Architect

myth: The wife of Rama, found in a furrow of the earth, who endured exile and captivity with steadfast virtue and at last returned into the earth; she is revered as an avatar of Lakshmi.
wants: Faith kept through hardship; those wrongly doubted given their due

myth: The cowherd maiden of Vrindavan, Krishna's beloved, revered as the embodiment of selfless devotional love.
wants: Devotion offered freely, without asking anything in return

myth: Son of Surya and the planet Saturn, a slow and stern judge who brings every being the fruit of their deeds; he is worshipped to soften hardship.
wants: Hard work done patiently; debts of deed paid without complaint

myth: The Vedic goddess of dawn, praised in many hymns of the Rigveda, who opens the gates of heaven each morning in a chariot of light and wakes all living things.
wants: Early rising and fresh starts; hymns sung at first light

myth: The fourth avatar of Vishnu, half man and half lion, who burst from a pillar at twilight to destroy the demon king Hiranyakashipu and protect his devotee Prahlada.
wants: Devotees protected, however clever the tyrant's defences

myth: An avatar of Vishnu who rose from the churning of the ocean carrying the pot of amrita, honoured as the father of Ayurveda.
wants: The sick treated without regard to rank; herbal lore recorded and shared

myth: A form of Parvati who holds a ladle and a bowl of food and feeds all who come to her, teaching that no one should go hungry.
wants: No guest turned away hungry; grain shared in hard seasons

n: Huitzilopochtli - God of the Sun and War
myth: Patron god of the Mexica, born fully armed from Coatlicue to defend her against his sister Coyolxauhqui; he led his people on their long migration to found Tenochtitlan.
wants: His people protected and led to new homes; the sun's daily battle fought

myth: Powerful god of the night sky, sorcery, fate and rulership, rival of Quetzalcoatl, who sees all things in his obsidian mirror and tests mortals with temptation.
wants: Pride tested and exposed; rulers reminded that fortune can turn

myth: Skeletal lord of Mictlan, the lowest level of the underworld, who rules the dead beside his wife and tried to stop Quetzalcoatl taking the bones to make new humans.
wants: The dead given grave goods for their journey; bones left undisturbed

myth: Queen of Mictlan who watches over the bones of the dead; her festivals for the departed live on in the Day of the Dead.
wants: The departed remembered with feasts and flowers each year

n: Xochiquetzal - Goddess of Flowers and Beauty
myth: Goddess of beauty, flowers, love and the crafts of weaving and embroidery, protector of young mothers and artisans.
wants: Beautiful things woven and grown; artisans and new mothers protected

myth: Earth mother goddess in a skirt of serpents, who conceived from a ball of feathers and gave birth to Huitzilopochtli as her other children came to kill her.
wants: Mothers defended; the earth fed in return for what it gives

myth: Goddess of desire, filth and purification, called the Eater of Filth because she hears confessions and cleanses wrongdoing.
wants: Wrongs confessed and cleansed; shame lifted from the repentant

n: Xolotl - God of Lightning and Death
myth: The dog-headed twin of Quetzalcoatl, god of lightning, fire and the misshapen, who guides the dead through Mictlan and helped carry back the bones that made humanity.
wants: The dead guided safely; the misshapen and outcast treated with respect

myth: The young god of maize, born of the earth goddess, from whose body the crops that feed the people arose.
wants: Fields planted and tended; maize honoured and never wasted

myth: Goddess of hearth fires and volcanoes, guardian of the home and its treasures, who was turned into a dog for breaking a fast.
wants: Hearths kept burning; household valuables guarded

myth: The Cloud Serpent, god of the hunt and the Milky Way, who first struck fire from flint and is a father of Quetzalcoatl in some tellings.
wants: Game hunted with skill and respect; the stars watched

myth: Sister of Huitzilopochtli who led her four hundred brothers against their mother and was cut down by him; her head became the moon.
wants: Defiance of an unjust order; the night given its due against the sun

myth: The old god of fire, day and time who sits at the centre of the world; the New Fire ceremony renewed him every fifty-two years.
wants: Fires renewed on schedule; the cycle of years honoured

myth: The dual creator, both male and female, who dwells in the highest heaven and is the source of all other gods.
wants: Balance kept between opposites; children born and named well

myth: Goddess of the maguey plant, whose sap makes pulque; her four hundred rabbit children are the spirits of drunkenness.
wants: Feasts shared in measure; the maguey and its gifts tended carefully

myth: A fearsome warrior goddess with wings edged in obsidian blades, ruler of the paradise of Tamoanchan and leader of the star-demons.
wants: Battle wounds honoured; women who die in childbirth revered as warriors

myth: God of art, games, music, dance, flowers and song, and twin of Xochiquetzal.
wants: Songs, dances and games offered with joy

myth: Trickster god of music, dance and storytelling, a shapeshifting coyote whose pranks often backfire on himself.
wants: Pranks played on the pompous; stories told late into the night

myth: Seven Serpent, goddess of maize and nourishment who carries ears of corn and keeps the people fed through the year.
wants: Seed corn saved and granaries filled for lean years

myth: The great earth creature torn apart by Quetzalcoatl and Tezcatlipoca to make the land and sky; her body is the world, and she hungers for what it gives back.
wants: What is taken from the land given back to it

myth: Lord of the vanguard and patron of the pochteca, the long-distance merchants who travelled with staffs he blessed.
wants: Caravans returned safely; trade routes opened and kept fair

n: Izanami - Goddess of Creation and Death
myth: Co-creator of the islands of Japan with Izanagi; she died giving birth to the fire god and became queen of Yomi, the land of the dead.
wants: The boundary between the living and the dead respected

myth: The god of thunder and lightning, shown ringed by drums that he beats to make storms.
wants: Storms respected; drummers and brave hearts honoured

myth: The god of wind who carries a great bag of winds over his shoulders, often shown beside Raijin.
wants: Foul air blown away; sailors and millers given their wind

n: Hachiman - God of Warriors and Archery
myth: Divine protector of Japan and of warriors, patron of the samurai, identified with the deified Emperor Ojin.
wants: Lands defended honourably; archery practised with discipline

n: Ryujin - Dragon King of the Sea
myth: The dragon god of the sea who lives in a coral palace beneath the waves and rules the tides with his magic jewels.
wants: Offerings made at sea; drowned sailors returned to their families

n: Ebisu - God of Fishermen and Luck
myth: Cheerful god of fishermen, good fortune and commerce, one of the Seven Lucky Gods, shown with a fishing rod and a large sea bream.
wants: Honest trade and generous catches; laughter at the market

n: Benzaiten - Goddess of Music and Eloquence
myth: Goddess of all that flows, water, words, music and wealth, adapted from Saraswati; one of the Seven Lucky Gods, she plays the biwa lute.
wants: Music played well and words spoken gracefully

myth: The fire god whose birth burned his mother Izanami to death; his grieving father slew him, and other gods sprang from his blood.
wants: Fire respected and controlled; smiths and kilns honoured

n: Takemikazuchi - God of Thunder and Swords
myth: Thunder and sword god born from Kagutsuchi's blood, who subdued Izumo for the heavenly gods and is said to pin down the earthquake catfish.
wants: Swords kept sharp and honourable; earthquakes held down

myth: A towering earthly god who met the heavenly grandson Ninigi at the crossroads of heaven and guided him down to earth; patron of guidance and new paths.
wants: Travellers guided safely; the lost shown the right road

n: Uzume - Goddess of Mirth and Dance
myth: Goddess of mirth and dance whose wild dance before the rock cave made the gods laugh and drew Amaterasu out, returning light to the world.
wants: Laughter where there is despair; dances and festivals performed

myth: Ruler and builder of the land of Izumo, kind to the white hare of Inaba; god of nation-building, medicine, farming and good marriages.
wants: Lands built up; good matches made and the wounded tended

myth: The deified scholar-statesman Sugawara no Michizane, whose wrath after unjust exile brought storms on the capital; now the patron of learning and examinations.
wants: Diligent study; the slandered and exiled vindicated

n: Daikokuten - God of Wealth and the Harvest
myth: One of the Seven Lucky Gods, a smiling god of wealth, farmers and kitchens who stands on rice bales holding a magic mallet.
wants: Kitchens stocked; hard work rewarded with prosperity

n: Bishamonten - God of Warriors and Treasure
myth: Armoured guardian of the north and of the Buddhist teaching, one of the Seven Lucky Gods, who protects the righteous and carries a pagoda of treasure.
wants: Temples and treasures guarded; righteous fighters armoured

myth: The wise counsellor of the heavenly gods who devised the plan of mirror, jewels and dance that drew Amaterasu from her cave.
wants: Problems solved with clever plans rather than force

myth: The blossom princess, wife of Ninigi, who gave birth inside a burning hut to prove her faithfulness; goddess of Mount Fuji and of volcanoes.
wants: Blossoms and mountains honoured; the faithful trusted

myth: Grandson of Amaterasu, sent down to rule the earth bearing the mirror, sword and jewel; ancestor of the imperial line.
wants: Heirs raised to rule well; regalia kept safe

myth: Goddess of food, agriculture and industry, enshrined in the outer shrine at Ise to provide Amaterasu's meals.
wants: Meals prepared with care; crops and crafts both honoured

myth: The laughing, round-bellied wandering monk of the Seven Lucky Gods, carrying a cloth sack of gifts; patron of happiness, children and contentment.
wants: Gifts given freely; worry let go

myth: The tall-browed Lucky God of happiness, wealth and long life, often shown with a crane and a staff tied with a scroll.
wants: Elders honoured and their knowledge kept

myth: Patron god of Babylon who became king of the gods by defeating the chaos-monster of the primordial sea and ordering the world from its body.
wants: Order imposed on chaos; cities governed by written law

myth: Queen of Kur, the land of no return, and elder sister of Inanna, whom she struck dead when Inanna descended through her seven gates.
wants: The laws of the underworld obeyed; her grief given a hearing

n: Nergal - God of Plague and War
myth: God of war, pestilence and the scorching midday sun, who forced his way into the underworld and became Ereshkigal's consort and co-ruler.
wants: Enemies laid low by fever and sword; the court below respected

myth: The moon god of Ur, also called Sin, who sails the night sky in a crescent boat and is the father of Utu and Inanna.
wants: Months reckoned correctly; herds tended under the moon

myth: Mother goddess of the mountains and of birth, who made the plants of Dilmun and healed Enki when he sickened from eating them.
wants: Births attended; mountain pastures kept fertile

n: Ninurta - God of the Plough and War
myth: Warrior and farmer god who defeated the monster Asag and the bird Anzu, recovering the Tablet of Destinies, and taught people to farm.
wants: Monsters hunted down; fields ploughed and irrigated

myth: Chief god of the Assyrians, the deified city of Ashur, worshipped as king of the gods and protector of the empire, often shown in a winged disc.
wants: Kingdoms expanded and defended under a strong crown

myth: Shepherd god and husband of Inanna, taken to the underworld in her place; he spends half of each year below while his sister Geshtinanna takes the other half.
wants: Flocks tended; the cycle of loss and return mourned and celebrated

myth: Son of Marduk and god of writing, scribes and wisdom, who inscribes the fates of all on the Tablet of Destinies.
wants: Records written and preserved; scribes trained

myth: The storm god, also called Adad, who brings rain to the fields and floods to the wicked, riding a bull and holding forked lightning.
wants: Rain on the faithful's fields; floods on oath-breakers

myth: Wife of Enlil, goddess of the air and grain, who followed him into the underworld and there bore the moon god Nanna.
wants: Spouses who follow each other anywhere; grain winnowed clean

n: Nisaba - Goddess of Writing and Grain
myth: Goddess of grain and the first patron of writing, accounting and surveying, who holds a golden stylus.
wants: Accounts kept honest; harvests measured fairly

myth: Goddess of healing and medicine, the great physician, often shown with her dog.
wants: Healers protected; dogs and the sick treated with kindness

n: Nanshe - Goddess of Justice and Dreams
myth: Goddess of Lagash who interpreted dreams, cared for orphans, widows and the poor, and protected the fish and birds of the marshes.
wants: Orphans and widows protected; fair weights kept in the market

n: Ningishzida - Lord of the Good Tree
myth: Serpent god of vegetation and the underworld and guardian at the gate of heaven, whose entwined snakes became a sign of healing.
wants: Trees planted and tended; the gates between worlds guarded

myth: Dumuzi's sister, goddess of wine, dreams and scribes, who would not betray her brother and shares his time in the underworld.
wants: Kin defended at any cost; wine and dreams shared

myth: The Great Lady, goddess of reeds and wife of Nanna, mother of Utu and Inanna, who lamented the destruction of her city Ur.
wants: Cities mourned and rebuilt; the troubled comforted

myth: Fire god and vizier of Enlil, the lamp that lights the night and burns away sorcery.
wants: Lamps lit in dark places; witchcraft burned out

n: Girra - God of the Refining Fire
myth: Fire god who purifies metals, bricks and evildoers, invoked against witches and curses.
wants: Metal refined and bricks fired; curses burned away
